text:
## Observations

1. An array indexed by initial rating can track the current rating for every possible query.
2. A contest preserves the nondecreasing order of current ratings, even when two adjacent ratings become equal.
3. In a nondecreasing array, the ratings in the inclusive interval \([L_i,R_i]\) occupy the half-open index range from the first rating at least \(L_i\) to the first rating at least \(R_i+1\).
4. A segment tree can use subtree maxima to find the first rating that reaches a threshold and lazy propagation to add one to an entire index range.
5. After the last contest, a single traversal can recover all final ratings for constant-time query lookups.

## Solution sketch

1. “An array indexed by initial rating can track the current rating for every possible query.” Let \(M=500{,}000\). Build a segment tree over indices \(1\) through \(M\), with leaf \(x\) initialized to rating \(x\). Store the maximum current rating and a pending addition at each node.

2. “A contest preserves the nondecreasing order of current ratings, even when two adjacent ratings become equal.” Process contests in input order. Equal ratings receive the same update. If two integer ratings satisfy \(a<b\), the smaller can increase to at most \(a+1\le b\), and the larger cannot decrease. Thus the array remains sorted after every contest.

3. “In a nondecreasing array, the ratings in the inclusive interval \([L_i,R_i]\) occupy the half-open index range from the first rating at least \(L_i\) to the first rating at least \(R_i+1\).” Find both indices before applying the contest update. Use \(M+1\) when a threshold exceeds the root maximum. If the two indices coincide, skip the update. Otherwise, add one from the first index up to but excluding the second. This also handles a single eligible rating value and ranges that reach the last leaf.

4. “A segment tree can use subtree maxima to find the first rating that reaches a threshold and lazy propagation to add one to an entire index range.” During a threshold search, push pending additions to the children before inspecting their maxima. Descend left if the left maximum reaches the threshold, and right otherwise. For a range addition, update the maximum and pending addition of each fully covered node. At partially covered nodes, push pending additions before descending and recompute the maximum afterward. Both searches and the range addition take \(O(\log M)\) time per contest.

5. “After the last contest, a single traversal can recover all final ratings for constant-time query lookups.” Push pending additions down to the leaves and store each leaf’s final rating by its initial index. For each query \(X\), print the value at index \(X\) in input order. Ratings can exceed \(M\) because the bound applies to the indices and the initial ratings. Building and traversing the tree each take \(O(M)\) time, so the total time is \(O(M+N\log M+Q)\), with \(O(M)\) auxiliary space when processing input and output incrementally.

generation.note: Harness wall time includes Codex startup; not API latency.

usage.note: Codex token counts include its harness context; not comparable to API usage.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
